parsed.explanation: No civilian statute targets trans people; the military criminalisation and trans exclusion are inapplicable to visitors. Documented exposures are societal hostility (organised violent anti-Pride attacks, one with police inaction), a state-facilitated outing incident (COVID contact-tracing doxing), a hospitalisation 'blind spot' with ministry refusal of guidance, and pervasive local discrimination. Mitigating: courts demonstrably work FOR trans people — final restroom ruling with compensation, surgery-requirement struck down, posthumous reinstatement — and travel material describes capital LGBTQ districts as broadly positive. Worst documented feature is tier-3 hostility with partially functioning recourse, not tier-1 state exposure. No border, document, facility, custody or police-profiling friction against visitors is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: None documented; no marker-mismatch friction, secondary screening, or entry refusal reported.
entry_documents.protection: Travel material describes broadly positive visitor experience in capital LGBTQ districts.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitors use home passports; local LGR regime not reachable by them.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Military statute criminalising same-sex conduct (up to 2 years) applies only to service members; trans people excluded from military. Civilian trans-prisoner housing undocumented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Military regime cannot reach a visitor; thin-data but no structural criminalisation of civilians to extrapolate from.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Human rights commission flagged a 'transgender blind spot in hospitalisation'; ministry refused to draft hospitalisation guidelines — a care-gap exposure if a visitor is hospitalised.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 2024 constitutional ruling on same-sex partners' healthcare rights; 2024 court struck mandatory-surgery condition.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Ward placement practice undocumented; gap is administrative reluctance, not a ban.

care_services.exposure: Survey (June 2025) documents pervasive discrimination burden in transition-related care; rural/urban applicability of the 2024 surgery ruling unresolved.
care_services.protection: Courts have ruled against surgery prerequisites, signalling some judicial protection of trans bodily autonomy.
care_services.interaction: Local-sphere data; visitors' emergency care exposure limited to the hospitalisation blind spot.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police advised a trans woman to avoid public restrooms — rights-infringing official conduct; one Pride attack met with alleged police inaction; no national GI anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Final, unappealed 2024 court ruling awarded compensation against the state; police protection (2,000 officers) at another Pride.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police conduct is reviewable and has been found unlawful by final judgment — recourse exists but is reactive.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans teens avoid school restrooms fearing outing; high youth harassment and conversion-therapy exposure — resident-facing, not visitor-facing. Travelling-with-minor exposure not documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Researchers' reform calls are aims, not law.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visitor with a minor faces no documented school/facility rule; no child-specific border or facility rule documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Organised, sometimes violent anti-LGBT protest: ~1,000 attackers at one Pride with alleged police inaction; 2020 entertainment-district tracing doxing and harassment; a trans man felt threatened on the street.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Robust policing at a second Pride; free media and civil society; no documented trans killings or visitor-targeted violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence clusters at public events; ordinary visitor districts described positively.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive GI anti-discrimination law; NGO registration met years of bureaucratic obstruction; tracing-doxing shows state outing capacity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working courts: compensation awarded, discharge ruled unjust and posthumously reinstated, surgery requirement struck down — rule of law demonstrably operating FOR trans people.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved: scope of the 2024 ruling; civilian prison placement practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Unlike Vellandra's universal visitor register and discretionary exclusion, this jurisdiction has no visitor-facing restriction at all; its worst state conduct is a bad police advisory and a doxing incident, both judicially correctable. Far above 0.35.

Like Kestrel Isles, harms are mostly discretionary and administrative with slow remedies; but here there is no documented border screening exposure at all, and courts issue final pro-trans rulings with compensation — slightly above the 0.55 tier.

Below Meridia-style 0.75: no comprehensive anti-discrimination statute, organised violent protest with one documented police-inaction episode, a ministry refusing trans hospitalisation guidance, and a state doxing incident — a genuinely more hostile climate than the 0.75 tier.

Comparable tier: brief hostile treatment, court-ordered release/compensation, uneven enforcement, broadly safe everyday travel in main areas; the marginally more organised opposition and data-doxing risk keep it at the upper 0.65 band rather than above it.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime contains no trans-specific criminal law a visitor can trigger: the military statute and service exclusion are structurally unreachable by a tourist, and no border, document, facility or custody rule touches visitors in the record. The operative exposures are societal hostility with episodic state lapses — violent counter-protest at Pride, one police-inaction episode, a discriminatory police advisory (corrected by final judgment with compensation), a COVID tracing-doxing event, and a healthcare/hospitalisation blind spot the ministry declined to address. Recourse is partially effective: courts have repeatedly ruled for trans plaintiffs, including posthumously and on bodily integrity. That places the worst documented feature at tier 3 (hostility with imperfect but real recourse), not tier 1 or 2. With travel material rating the capital's LGBTQ districts broadly positive and no documented visitor-targeted violence, the case sits at the top of the Elevated band: 0.68.
